column3: “In your hand” is rendered “with you,” and NASB adds “some.”
“Acting as a stranger” is rendered “pretend to be another woman.”
“Sent to you hard” is rendered “sent to you with a harsh message.”
“Raised you up” is rendered “exalted you,” and “ruler” as “leader.”
“One who urinates on a wall” is rendered “every male person,” and “shut up and freed” as “both bond and free.” NASB renders “sweep away behind” as “make a clean sweep of.”
“Open country” is rendered “field,” and NASB supplies “it.”
The Hebrew ending (“this the day, and what? also now”) is obscure; NASB renders “this day and from now on.”
NASB supplies “Euphrates,” and renders “Asherah poles” as “Asherim.”
“The scroll of the matters of the days” is rendered “the Book of the Chronicles.”
“Made Him jealous” is rendered “provoked Him to jealousy.”
“Runners” is rendered “the guard,” and “on the hand of” as “to the care of.”
